title: My hamster ARPG has a full trailer now, and some answers about how I'm making it
author: Tap_Little
selftext:
Thanks for the response to my last clip. A few people asked about the terrain, fire effects, sound, and which AI tools I'm using, so I wanted to answer those properly and share the new trailer for HAMSTER: CLAW.



I started this because I love hack-and-slash games like Diablo and wanted to make a lighter one of my own, with a tiny hamster fighting its way through a world that is much too big for it.



The engine is Godot. I'm using Codex Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 for coding and development, and I rely on AI throughout the process.



For the monsters and environments, I use Meshy AI. The terrain questions were probably the most common: I generate each floor's environment as a whole through Meshy, then add texture work where the result is missing detail. Those models are brought into Godot to become the game's maps. This is the approach I've been using so far; I don't know if it's how an experienced developer would do it.



The VFX and sound are a mix of AI and free assets licensed for commercial use. That's what I'm using for the spell effects, explosions, and audio people asked about.



This is my first game, so I'm learning as I go. Some of my methods may be wrong, and the game still has plenty of rough edges. I'm sharing what I've actually been doing, and I'd appreciate advice from people who've run into similar problems, especially with getting generated environments to work well in a game.



The Steam page is now live. The demo isn't available yet, but I'm working toward releasing it as soon as I can. If you'd like to try it when it's ready, you can wishlist it here:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5363820/HAMSTER\_CLAW/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5363820/HAMSTER_CLAW/)

comments.author: fuddlesworth
comments.body: How much cleanup are you doing manually for the models? I've found texture mapping and sometimes meshes to not be great.

replies.author: Tap_Little
replies.body:
I’m actually doing very little manual cleanup. I’ve been fixing pretty much everything through prompting and regeneration.

When I generate models with Meshy AI, I also spend a lot of time preparing the source images and trying to make them as close as possible to what I want in the final 3D model. That seems to help a lot with the mesh and textures.

comments.author: deReaLizedGames
comments.body:
Really cool! It's super creative. The part where he walked in the wheel got me laughing. Attack effects look really solid.

Two suggestions: work on polishing the animations. They're pretty stiff currently, and in an ARPG game feel + perceived quality is dictated significantly by the animations.

I'd also revisit the environments. There's currently a ton of brown, the ground is brown, the characters are brown, the props are brown. It looks a bit washed out.

Overall I think you're doing a great job and have something really cool here!

replies.author: Tap_Little
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback and the kind words! I’ll definitely work on making the animations smoother and breaking up all that brown so things stand out more. Really appreciate you taking the time to point those out.

replies.author: deReaLizedGames
replies.body: Can't wait to see how it progresses!
